hypothesis: the scaffold reproduces the sibling trees' accuracy exactly (same split, same model) and fails physics, because a tree is piecewise constant and saturates outside the 0.5 mi training range while the sweep runs to 5 mi
observation: rmse 0.013345 / trip_rmse 0.003037, identical to both sibling trees; 6 of 9 checks fail, led by climb_floor at 81.1% and round_trip_convexity at 45.7%, with implied eta_drive 1.290 and length_invariance 8.83
reasoning: the dominant failure is not extrapolation but the grade response itself: an implied drivetrain efficiency of 1.29 means the forest bills a climb for less than the height it gains at every distance, so no amount of range extension fixes it - the functional form has to encode gravity

description: structured physics parametrization: 4 bounded heads (A,B,C,T) driven by an MLP
hypothesis: predicting E = d*(A + B*g+ - C*g-) + T with each head squashed into its physically legal interval satisfies all nine checks by construction, because the ceiling in physics.py decomposes into exactly the same d-proportional and d-fixed parts
observation: physics_pass 1.0 with every violation rate at 0.0 and length_invariance exactly 0.0, at rmse 0.013397 (+0.39%) and trip_rmse 0.003060 (+0.76%) against the unconstrained forest; 389s of the 600s budget
reasoning: the guarantee held algebraically on the first try, and the accuracy cost of being physically legal is under 1% even with the network seeing only speed - grade and length are carried entirely by the structure, so all the remaining capacity is free for information the baseline never had

description: add prev_speed_mph to the network inputs
hypothesis: acceleration is the dominant unmeasured driver of link energy (both sibling trees), and the T head is exactly the per-link transient energy, so the entry speed should feed it directly without needing a per-mile kinetic term
observation: rmse -19.3% and trip_rmse -1.7%, physics still passing on every check; length_invariance moved 0.0 -> 3.31 because T became non-zero
reasoning: the split is the classic information signature - a large rmse gain with almost none at trip level - and the length_invariance move is the structure working as intended, since a non-zero fixed cost T makes the per-mile rate genuinely higher on short links

description: add next_speed_mph (the exit half of the kinetic delta)
hypothesis: this tree has no one-link-lookback restriction, so the exit speed is available; the unguided tree's best single feature was two-sided, so the exit half should still carry signal after the entry half is in
observation: rmse -4.7% and trip_rmse -4.6%, moving together for the first time this session; physics still clean
reasoning: the exit-side gain is about a quarter of the entry-side gain, matching the sibling trees' 2-4x entry-over-exit ratio, and the fact that trip_rmse moved as far as rmse suggests the exit speed removes a *systematic* bias - links that end in braking were previously overbilled everywhere

hypothesis: prev_miles tells the model how much to trust prev_speed_mph as an estimate of the speed at the previous link's end, and was a top-3 feature in both sibling trees
observation: rmse -3.1% but trip_rmse +0.31%, so not Pareto-dominant; length_invariance collapsed 2.63 -> 0.59, meaning the model moved a lot of its explanation out of the fixed T term and into the per-mile rate A
reasoning: the length_invariance collapse is the tell: prev_miles lets the model resolve per-link error by re-attributing energy from T to A, which sharpens individual links but shifts a small systematic bias into every link of a trip at once - exactly the error mode trip_rmse is sensitive to; worth re-testing once something else has moved trip_rmse

hypothesis: the speed two links back describes how the vehicle approached, and was worth -4.6% in the unguided tree
observation: rmse -0.42% and trip_rmse +0.07%, so a near-tie that is not Pareto-dominant
reasoning: worth ten times less here than in the unguided tree, and the reason is structural: there the second-order approach information had to be inferred from raw speeds, while here T is already an explicit per-link transient energy that prev_speed and next_speed pin down directly - the second-order term has almost nothing left to add

description: let the climb term spend the flat rate's unused ceiling headroom
hypothesis: pinning the climb slope to [k_pot, k_pot/eta_peak] says a climb never costs more than mgh at peak drivetrain efficiency, but a real climb runs the motor off its peak; if that bound binds it is a signed bias on every graded link, which is exactly what trip_rmse punishes
observation: both metrics improved but only by ~0.15%; implied_eta_drive moved from 1.000 (pinned at the old bound) to 0.895, so the extra headroom is genuinely being spent
reasoning: keep, but the small size is the more useful result: the climb slope was barely binding, so the remaining trip_rmse error is not in the grade response - the diagnostic value of this experiment exceeded its accuracy value

description: signed transient: let a link give back the kinetic energy it releases
hypothesis: with T >= 0 and A >= res/2, a flat link could never be predicted below half its road load, yet a quarter of the data is at or below zero - the model was structurally unable to express regen, and gating a negative T on the kinetic energy actually released (zero at steady state, so zero on the sweep) unlocks it without touching the guarantee
observation: rmse -26.2% and trip_rmse -14.9%, the largest move of the session, with every physics check still passing
reasoning: this was a missing *sign*, not missing information - the same three speeds were already inputs, and all that changed is that the structure now lets their difference come out negative; the lesson is to audit a constrained parametrization for what it cannot represent before adding features to it

description: re-test prev_miles under the signed-transient structure
hypothesis: prev_miles was discarded at exp4 for a 0.31% trip_rmse regression, and the sibling trees' rule is that a marginal feature is tuned against an architecture rather than against the problem; the signed transient changed the architecture materially, so it should be re-measured
observation: rmse -8.8% and trip_rmse -5.1%, where the same feature previously bought -3.1% rmse at the cost of trip_rmse
reasoning: prev_miles says how much to trust prev_speed as the speed at the previous link's end, and that only pays once the model has something quantitative to do with the entry speed - before exp7 it could only add energy, so a sharper entry estimate had nowhere useful to go
